title: Add Minimum Number of Rungs
statement:
A ladder has rungs at the heights listed in `rungs`, a strictly increasing array of integers. You start on the floor at height `0` and want to reach the highest rung, `rungs[rungs.length - 1]`.

From where you stand (the floor or a rung) you may move up to the next rung above you only if it is at most `dist` higher than your current height. You may add new rungs at any positive integer heights that do not already hold a rung.

Return the smallest number of rungs you have to add so that the last rung becomes reachable.
notes:
## Intuition

Each gap between consecutive heights (starting from the floor at `0`) can be handled on its own: rungs added inside one gap never help another. Inside a gap, the best a single climb can do is `dist`, so the greedy choice is to place each new rung exactly `dist` above the last one. A brute force simulates those steps one by one, which is too slow when the gap is `10^9` and `dist` is `1`; a division counts them at once.

A gap of length `gap` is covered by `ceil(gap / dist)` climbs, so it needs `ceil(gap / dist) - 1` new rungs, which equals `floor((gap - 1) / dist)`.

## Approach

1. Set `added = 0` and `previous = 0` (the floor).
2. For each `height` in `rungs`, compute `gap = height - previous`.
3. Add `Math.floor((gap - 1) / dist)` to `added`.
4. Move `previous` up to `height` and continue; return `added`.

## Example 1, step by step

`rungs = [1, 3, 5, 10]`, `dist = 2`.

| height | gap | (gap - 1) / dist, floored | added |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| 5 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| 10 | 5 | 2 | 2 |

Only the last gap of 5 needs help: rungs at 7 and 9 (or 7 and 8) do it, so the answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one constant-time step per rung.
- Space: O(1): a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Do not forget the first gap from the floor at height `0`.
- Use `(gap - 1) / dist`, not `gap / dist`: a gap of exactly `dist` needs no new rung.
- Simulating one rung at a time can mean `10^9` steps; use the division.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `added` | rungs inserted so far |
| `previous` | height you are standing on before the next rung (starts at the floor, `0`) |
| `height` | the next existing rung |
| `gap` | distance from `previous` up to `height` |

narration.2: No rungs have been added yet.
narration.3: You start on the floor, at height 0.
narration.5: Visit the existing rungs from lowest to highest.
narration.6: Measure how far the next rung is above where you stand.
narration.7: A gap needs ceil(gap / dist) climbs, so floor((gap - 1) / dist) new rungs placed dist apart.
narration.8: Climb onto this rung; the next gap is measured from here.
narration.10: Every gap has been bridged with the fewest rungs; return the total.
